Theme

## Philosophy quotes about society

Society is the web of institutions, customs, and mutual expectations in which individual freedom takes shape.

32 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

### Why this theme matters

Social philosophy asks how individuals and collectives constitute each other, and what justice requires of shared life.

### In the history of philosophy

From classical politics and Confucian relational ethics to contract theory, sociology, and critical theory, society is both fact and project.

### Thinkers in this collection

[Jean-Jacques Rousseau](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jean-jacques-rousseau) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [Hu Shi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/hu-shi) , [Guanzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/guanzi) , [Qian Mu](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/qian-mu) , [Ibn Khaldun](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ibn-khaldun) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne) , [David Hume](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/david-hume)

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is society in philosophy?

It is the organized coexistence of persons through norms, institutions, and shared meanings.

#### Do individuals exist before society?

Some theories start from individuals; others hold that persons are formed within social relations from the start.

#### Where are philosophy quotes about society?

Browse this theme alongside politics, justice, and power.
